timeline: Vienna's maternity clinic lost eighteen percent of mothers before Ignaz Semmelweis enforced handwashing, but his peers rewarded him with an asylum.
Doctors dissected cadavers in autopsy rooms.
They delivered babies without washing hands.
Semmelweis ordered chlorinated lime basin washings.
Maternal mortality plummeted under two percent.
Outraged physicians mocked his hygienic discovery.
Colleagues committed him to an asylum.
Guards beat him, and he died days later from sepsis possibly caused by the injuries.
Germ theory later proved him right.
Yet medical arrogance silenced the truth for decades.
